theorem ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightEncodedColorResult.meets {pMain prime cover wanted controls bank out len p : ℕ} {μ : ℕ → ℤ}
    (main : P[pMain]?=some _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightEncodedColorResult.body) (hw : (lim.space : ℤ) ≤ lim.word)
    (hprime : prime ≤ out) (hcover : cover ≤ out) (hwanted : wanted ≤ out)
    (hcontrols : controls ≤ out) (hbank : bank ≤ out)
    (hspace : out+8 ≤ lim.space) (hlen : (len : ℤ) ≤ lim.word) (hp : (p : ℤ) ≤ lim.word) :
    _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Meets lim P pMain d [prime,cover,wanted,controls,bank,out,len,p] μ 600
      (fun r ν => r=(out : ℤ) ∧ _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Seg ν out (_root_.ThreeSum.LightEncodedColorResult.values prime cover wanted controls bank out len p) ∧ _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Kept μ ν out) := by sorry
natural_language_statement:
Suppose the prime, cover, wanted, control, and bank pointers precede output address $o$, eight output cells fit, the length and modulus fit words, and addresses fit words. The result-header procedure returns $o$ in at most 600 light steps, writes the specified eight-cell record, and preserves memory below $o$.

This record-writing contract exposes the completed selected-color pipeline through actual stored pointers and counts.
